concession-01.why: la pluie is a noun, so malgré + noun. bien que and même si need a clause.

concession-02.why: bien que + subjunctive: qu’il soit tard. est and sera are indicative, only for même si.

concession-03.why: même si + indicative: le billet est cher. soit is subjunctive (for bien que); serait is conditional, which can’t follow même si.

concession-04.why: The fixed structure avoir beau + infinitive (however much…, it’s no use): il a beau répéter. être beau / faire beau mean something else (to be handsome, to be fine weather).

concession-05.why: Contrasting facts about two people takes tandis que + an indicative clause. malgré and en dépit de can only take a noun.

concession-06.why: Cheap yet very tasty, contrary to expectation, so pourtant (yet). donc expresses a result and parce que a cause; neither expresses contrast.

concession-07.why: Only a noun phrase follows (critiques), with no verb, so en dépit de + les = en dépit des. bien que and même si need a clause with a conjugated verb.

concession-08.why: quoique (= bien que) + subjunctive: qu’elle ait. a and aura are indicative.

concession-09.why: A full clause follows (la météo avait annoncé…), so alors que + indicative for contrast. malgré and en dépit de can only take a noun.

concession-10.why: avoir beau takes an infinitive: elle a beau faire des économies. fait is a conjugated form or past participle and faisant a present participle; neither can follow avoir beau.

concession-11.why: certes… mais is the fixed “concede, then rebut” structure. pourtant already expresses contrast and would double up with the mais that follows; malgré needs a noun.

concession-12.why: il n’empêche que (nevertheless) takes the indicative: il est indispensable. soit is subjunctive; être is the infinitive.

concession-13.why: même si + plus-que-parfait expresses a hypothesis contrary to past fact (the main clause is in the past conditional). serions partis is conditional, not used after même si; soyons partis is subjunctive.

concession-14.why: bien que + past subjunctive (the action is complete): qu’ils aient essayé. ont is indicative; auraient is conditional.

concession-15.why: cependant (however) at the start links two independent sentences, expressing a limitation or contrast. malgré needs a noun; bien que needs a subjunctive clause and can’t just be followed by a comma.

concession-16.why: The verb in the clause is the subjunctive ait, so only bien que works. malgré takes a noun; même si takes the indicative (même s’il a beaucoup travaillé).

concession-17.why: Better qualified yet earning less, contrary to expectation, so pourtant. puisque expresses a cause and si bien que a result; neither is logical.

concession-18.why: même si takes the present indicative, even when referring to the future: même s’il pleut demain. pleuve is subjunctive; pleuvra is the future, which can’t follow si.

concession-19.why: avoir beau in the passé composé: nous avons eu beau chercher. être can’t replace avoir: sommes beau / avons été beau are both wrong.

concession-20.why: The clause uses the indicative connaît, so alors que (whereas, yet) for contrast. malgré takes a noun; bien que requires the subjunctive (bien qu’il connaisse).

concession-21.why: quoi que (two words) = whatever, the object of dises. quoique (= bien que) and bien que mean “although” and would leave the sentence without an object, incomplete.

concession-22.why: The fixed expression il n’empêche que + indicative, with no pas. il n’empêche pas que is a common error; qu’à isn’t a structure.

concession-23.why: certes introduces the concession and mais introduces the rebuttal in the second half: certes…, mais…. donc expresses a result and car a cause; neither forms a concessive structure.

concession-24.why: A noun phrase follows, so en dépit de + noun (de + de nombreuses → de nombreuses). bien que and alors que need a clause.

concession-25.why: soit is subjunctive, so it needs quoique / bien que (written register). même si and alors que take the indicative.

concession-26.why: même si + imparfait expresses a hypothesis contrary to present fact, with the conditional in the main clause: Même si j’avais le temps, je ne partirais pas. aurais is conditional and aie subjunctive; neither can follow même si.

concession-27.why: avoir beau must match the tense of the main clause: the main clause is in the imparfait (refusait), so elle avait beau insister. était uses the wrong auxiliary; a is present and doesn’t fit a past narrative.

concession-28.why: même si + indicative (a real past fact): elle a travaillé. ait travaillé is subjunctive and aurait travaillé conditional; neither can follow même si.

concession-29.why: avoir beau takes an infinitive, the past infinitive for a completed action: avoir fait. ayant fait is a compound participle and qu’il ait fait a clause; neither can follow avoir beau.

concession-30.why: The adverb néanmoins (nevertheless) can go between the auxiliary/modal and the infinitive. malgré needs a noun; bien que must introduce a clause.
